title: First start on the LS, now the 12A will not be rebuilt?
ask: With the 12A not being rebuilt, should the new wiring wait to be started and proven on the LS instead of on the 12A?
why:
The plan starts the new wiring on the 12A first: today's rotary engine leg is eleven wires on L1-E1 (D-606), the first start and the charging and voltage-drop checks are E12, and the shakedown drives come before the swap. Camden has ruled the 12A will not be rebuilt (03-engine, 2026-10-16). If it never runs again, building that rotary leg and the 12A start steps is wasted work. If the noise turns out to be the starter, the 12A could run again cheaply and keep the car moving until the LS is in.

Today's facts (00-CAR K-025): 3 psi at the fuel gauge, a carburettor inlet leak fixed, it cranked fast on the Ionic and made a loud metal screech. Nobody has found where the noise comes from (the starter or the engine), and no compression test has been done.
options:
(a) LS first. The 12A comes out as it is and is sold as a core. Today's rotary engine leg is not built, and the first start, the charging checks and the shakedown drives move to after the LS runs. Costs nothing extra. The car cannot move under its own power until the LS is in.
(b) Find the noise first, then decide. A free check of about an hour: plugs out, gearbox in N, turn the engine by hand with a socket on the big bolt in the middle of the front pulley. If it turns smoothly and quietly, the screech is most likely the starter: a starter gets the 12A running on the new wiring until the swap, and it sells as a running engine. If it binds or grinds, it is the engine, and (a) follows.
(c) Keep the 12A plan with a used running 12A in its place. It costs money and an engine swap for an engine that leaves again at the LS swap.
recommend: (b), unless you want to spend no more time on the 12A at all - then (a).
stops: The build track's rewrite (Y76): whether it keeps today's rotary engine leg and the first start on the 12A (E12) or moves them to the LS; and whether the 12A is sold as a running engine or a dead one (03-engine CP01).
